text: 🇲🇽🇻🇪 264 Mexican rescuers decorated by Venezuela after two earthquakes: 80 bodies recovered, 2 pulled out alive, nearly 2,000 medical consults. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the humanitarian mission to Venezuela Mexico’s “Yumare” humanitarian group was honored by Venezuela’s government. 13.1 tons of medicine, 71.2 tons of supplies and 8 power generators delivered. Two more ships set sail yesterday — citizen collections and government aid.

🇲🇽🏭 “In these circumstances we’re doing well. People are better off. The peso, inflation — down. We keep moving forward.” — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the economy under Trump’s tariffs Despite Washington’s protectionist measures, Sheinbaum says the major indicators hold: stable peso, low inflation. She promised the second half of 2026 will show even more — days out from her second informe de gobierno.

🚨🇲🇽 Sheinbaum: the capture of “El Mayo” involved US interference — and she’s putting the whole timeline on the record. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Zambada operation Mexico’s Attorney General will present a detailed chronology — from García Luna to Zambada — showing how US agencies operated on the case. Her line: no foreign intervention overrides Mexican sovereignty or Mexican law.

🇲🇽📈 MEXICO'S INVESTMENT TURNS THE CORNER

Gross fixed investment rose 5.9% year-on-year in April, snapping a 17-month losing streak, INEGI reported today. Construction jumped 10.1% and — notably — public investment climbed 7.5%, outpacing the private sector's 5.7%. The "peso in crisis, capital fleeing" narrative keeps colliding with the data.

🇲🇽🛢️ PEMEX + PETROBRAS: SOUTH-SOUTH ENERGY, NO WASHINGTON REQUIRED

Sheinbaum announced Pemex will reopen deep-water exploration at Cantarell using Petrobras's technology, aiming to hold production near 1.8 million barrels a day. Two Latin American state oil companies sharing know-how to keep the fuel flowing — and she was explicit that strengthening output "does not replace" the energy transition, it runs alongside it. Cooperation and sovereignty, not privatization.

🇲🇽🤝 16.5 MILLION MEXICANS GET PAID THIS WEEK

Payments for the July–August cycle of the Bienestar pensions begin this week: 16,571,522 people — seniors, Mujeres Bienestar and people with disabilities — receiving direct deposits. No intermediaries, no means-tested humiliation. A right written into the constitution, paid directly to the people.

🇲🇽🏗️ 11.2 BILLION PESOS TO END THE FLOODS IN THE VALLEY OF MEXICO

Sheinbaum's government is putting 11,200 million pesos into hydraulic works to finally end the seasonal flooding that drowns the east of the Valley of Mexico every rainy season. Conagua presented the plan at today's mañanera — drainage and infrastructure for the communities that have paid decades of official neglect with their homes.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICO'S EXPORT BOOM IS ALSO A WARNING

Mexican electronics and computing exports exploded 95.6% year-on-year in Q1 to $50.078 billion — Chihuahua alone shipped $26 billion, up 119%. But INEGI's own numbers show the trap underneath: 92% of it goes to the United States and 96% is made in just five states. Banco Base's Gabriela Siller lays out three risks stacked on one buyer: "more than 90% of exports go to the United States, 67.25% of those imports go to Texas." The case for diversification writes itself.

🔥🇲🇽 GARCÍA LUNA'S PRISON-LOOTING NETWORK KEEPS FALLING

A federal judge just bound over Jesús Gabriel Pérez Rodríguez for embezzlement and criminal association — another node of Genaro García Luna's machine. The FGR says the ring diverted more than 5 billion pesos meant for federal prison upkeep under the ex-security secretary, laundering 2.95 billion through shell companies and fake invoices tied to the husband of TV host Inés Gómez Mont. Sixty people were charged in the same scheme.

TIME: U.S. Declines to Renew Trade Pact With Mexico and Canada — Here's What It Means
July 2, 2026 | 🟡

"Declines" — passive, tidy, blameless. It was Trump who refused the 16-year extension; the deal now drops into a decade of annual reviews. TIME leads with a "senior U.S. official" citing trade deficits and fear of Chinese firms using Mexico as a backdoor — US grievances first, the Mexican economy left hanging last. 8–13 million US jobs ride on this trade, yet the "uncertainty" is framed as everyone's, not Washington's choice.

Even the reassurance is on US terms: officials call the non-renewal "not a doomsday scenario" while pocketing the leverage of yearly reviews.
